question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution:
The correct answer is '**they decided**'.

 

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• The action of choosing to play with the frisbee occurred after eating, in the past, so the verb must be in the simple past tense.
 
• "**They decided**" correctly follows the past tense structure used throughout the passage.
 
• Other options are grammatically incorrect: "**everyone decide**" has a subject-verb mismatch, "**they had decide**" is incorrect past perfect (should be "had decided"), and "**they all decide**" is in present tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

Complete Passage: **Sarah and Tom love to go to the park on__ weekends. Last Sunday, they **__arranged__ a picnic basket with sandwiches, fruit, and juice. They **__brought__** a blanket to sit on and a frisbee to play with.*

*As soon as __they arrived__ at the park, Sarah spread the blanket on the green grass. They enjoyed their sandwiches and had juicy oranges. After eating, __they decided__ to play with the frisbee.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Everyone decide** – Incorrect subject-verb agreement.
 
• **They had decide** – Incorrect form of past perfect; should be "had decided".
 
• **They all decide** – Present tense; not suitable in a past narrative.
